title: Home-Cleaner Refill Concentrate Usage
dataSources: Carbon estimates (`carbon:estimate`), recycling weight (`recycling:weight`), food waste (`foodwaste:log`), repairs (`repair:event`).
app: Sustainability telemetry — carbon-footprint apps, home recycling scales, food-waste logs, and repair / reuse journals — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs, MQTT, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=recycling:weight stream=refill
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(eval(if(package_type="refill",kg,0))) as refill_kg, sum(eval(if(package_type="single_use",kg,0))) as single_use_kg by _time
| eval refill_share_pct=round(100*refill_kg/(refill_kg+single_use_kg),1)
| sort - _time
description: Compares refill or concentrate packaging with single-use cleaner packaging over time.
value: Refill systems only pay off if they become the dominant behavior, not an occasional exception.
implementation: Track cleaner packaging by type in a refill stream and chart monthly refill share percentage.
visualization: Line chart of refill versus single-use cleaner packaging share.

references.title: EPA — reducing wasted food at home

grandmaExplanation: It compares whether you are mostly using refills for household cleaners instead of buying new plastic each time.
